correctness.rationale: Expanding the published polynomial gives exactly \(D=(\{x_1=0\}\cup\{x_1=1\})\setminus\{0\}\). For an \(r\)-subcode with annihilator \(W\) of dimension \(h=n-r\), zero coordinates are precisely the defining-set columns and systematic basis columns contained in \(W\). If \(W\) lies in the hyperplane \(x_1=0\), the defining-set intersection has size \(3^h-1\); otherwise the nonzero first-coordinate functional has three equal fibers and the intersection has size \(2\cdot3^{h-1}-1\). Inclusion-exclusion over coordinate axes proves the stated \(E_{m,h}(s)\) counts. The minimizer comparison is strict by \(3^{h-1}\) for \(h\ge1\), and equality \(s=h\) forces a coordinate subspace in the hyperplane. Exhaustive replay for \(n=3,4,5\) agrees with every distribution formula and the source's \(n=3\) weight enumerator.

value.rationale: The primary paper introduces the family as a new infinite ternary LCD construction but records only one-dimensional weight data. The new theorem gives every higher support layer for every dimension and every family parameter \(n\), together with a simple geometric dichotomy and exact extremal multiplicities. This is substantially more informative than a finite example or a routine minimum-distance check: it resolves the full SSWD of an infinite newly published family and identifies all generalized-weight minimizers.
